facts.text: I have pain in my belly.
It's in the upper middle part of my belly, below the breastbone.
My urine has been dark, the colour of tea.

facts.item: how long the dark urine, pale stools and itching have lasted
facts.text: They've been going on for a week.
It came on after the dark urine, pale stools and itching had started.
It's all over: on my palms, the soles of my feet, my body, my face and my groin.
It's made of small raised bumps.
The whites of my eyes have turned yellow.
I don't have any significant medical problems.
I haven't taken any herbal supplements, not even over-the-counter ones.
I drink occasionally: 2–3 standard drinks on several days a month.
I'm a man who has sex with men.
Several months before I got sick, I had unprotected sex with multiple partners.

findings.name: skin examination
findings.result: Diffuse papular rash involving the palms, soles, trunk, face and groin.

findings.name: liver function tests
findings.result: Alkaline phosphatase 279 U/L; AST 70 U/L; ALT 167 U/L; total bilirubin 5.6 mg/dL (conjugated bilirubin 3.7 mg/dL); albumin 2.6 g/dL.

findings.name: autoimmune liver serology
findings.result: Antimitochondrial antibody positive (57 U); anti-smooth muscle antibody positive (31 U).

findings.name: viral hepatitis serology
findings.result: Hepatitis A, B and C negative.

findings.name: magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography
findings.result: Moderate intrahepatic biliary dilation; heterogeneous perfusion of the liver.

gold.reasoning: 1. Medication-induced cholestasis was considered but excluded based on history — “He denied taking any medications including over-the-counter herbal supplements or analgesics.” 2. Acute viral hepatitis was considered but excluded after testing — “Hepatitis screen was negative for acute hepatitis A, B, or C infection.” 3. Primary biliary cholangitis was considered given cholestatic injury and positive AMA but excluded because “In this case, the patient presented with features atypical of PBC, such as a diffuse rash along the palms and soles, biliary dilatation, evidence of glomerular injury, and a sudden onset of symptoms.” 4. Secondary syphilis was suspected based on rash and sexual risk factors — “Considering the patient's rash, the history of unprotected sex, and high-risk group (MSM), syphilis screening was performed.”

notes: Index visit: the emergency presentation with epigastric pain after a week of dark urine, pale stools and itching followed by a new rash (s001-s012).
